name: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
traveler: Professor Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land, aboard Captain Nemo's Nautilus
summary: Jules Verne's novel of 1869–70. Three men hunting a sea monster are taken aboard Captain Nemo's submarine and carried round the world under the sea in ten months: across the Pacific, under the Isthmus of Suez, to Atlantis, the South Pole and the Maelstrom. This is fiction. The route follows the positions and dates Aronnax logs, converted from Verne's Paris meridian, through real seas and a few places that never existed. It makes nothing known to anyone.

stops.note: The frigate Abraham Lincoln sails to hunt the 'monster' that has been holing ships. Aboard are Professor Aronnax of the Paris Museum, his servant Conseil and the harpooner Ned Land (Part 1, ch. 3–4).
Commander Farragut will not risk the Strait of Magellan, and doubles the Horn into the Pacific (Part 1, ch. 5).

Some 200 miles south of Japan, after three months of empty sea, a glow in the night. Ned's harpoon rings on metal, and the three men are thrown overboard onto the back of a submarine: the Nautilus (Part 1, ch. 5–7).
Captain Nemo takes his first noon sight, and sets course along the warm 'Black River' current. Aronnax will not see land for weeks (Part 1, ch. 13–14).
A hunt in Nemo's 'forests': the three walk the seabed in diving suits around an island Verne took from the charts of his day. It does not exist (Part 1, ch. 14–16).
Hawaii, where Cook died in 1779, slips past. The Nautilus has gone 4,860 leagues (Part 1, ch. 17).
The Marquesas, three miles off (Part 1, ch. 17).
Off a Tuamotu atoll Aronnax studies how coral builds islands (Part 1, ch. 18).
The Society Islands left to the east (Part 1, ch. 18).
Nemo shows where La Pérouse's ships were lost in 1788, and the box of papers he raised from the wreck (Part 1, ch. 18).
Aground on a reef off Gueboroar. The prisoners go ashore to hunt; Papuan canoes gather, and Nemo electrifies the hand-rail (Part 1, ch. 19–21).
Round the eastern point of the Gulf of Carpentaria (Part 1, ch. 22).
The prisoners are drugged and shut in. A crewman, hurt in the night, dies, and is buried in a coral grove on the seabed (Part 1, ch. 22–23).
Logged at noon: 12°5' S, 94°33' east of Paris (Part 2, ch. 1).
At the entrance to the Bay of Bengal, the Nautilus crosses a patch of luminous water after nightfall. Aronnax gives no bearings for it (Part 2, ch. 1).
Off Ceylon, a walk among the pearl oysters. Nemo kills a shark to save an Indian diver, and gives him a bag of pearls (Part 2, ch. 2–3).
Between the Maldives and the Laccadives (Part 2, ch. 4).
Past the fortress at the mouth of the Red Sea (Part 2, ch. 4).
Ned Land harpoons a dugong (Part 2, ch. 5).

Nemo's own passage under the Isthmus of Suez, found, he says, by tagging fish on both sides. In twenty minutes the Nautilus is off Port Said. No such tunnel exists; the canal opened in 1869 (Part 2, ch. 5).
'Scarpanto', the home of Proteus (Part 2, ch. 6).
A diver comes to the window, and Nemo sends him off with a chest of gold. Crete is in revolt against the Ottomans (Part 2, ch. 6).
The sea boils over a new volcanic island (Part 2, ch. 6).
The whole Mediterranean in forty-eight hours, by sunrise on the 18th (Part 2, ch. 7).
Nemo's crew walk the seabed, gathering gold from the Spanish galleons sunk here in 1702 (Part 2, ch. 8).
By night, on foot, to the ruins of a drowned city under a living volcano (Part 2, ch. 9).
The Nautilus enters an extinct volcano through a submerged passage to replenish its stores of sodium. Aronnax can only guess which Atlantic island shelters Nemo’s harbour (Part 2, ch. 10).
A day under a raft of weed and wreckage (Part 2, ch. 11).
Nemo sounds the South Atlantic and finds no bottom at 7,000 fathoms (Part 2, ch. 11).
Blocked by the pack. Nemo dives under it (Part 2, ch. 13).
Nemo takes the sun's altitude at noon of the equinox, and plants a black flag with a gold N. Real explorers reached the pole only in 1911 (Part 2, ch. 14).
An iceberg turns over and seals the Nautilus in. Five days of digging and boiling water, the air running out, before she rams her way free (Part 2, ch. 15–16).
North again (Part 2, ch. 17).
Land at last, too far for Ned to swim (Part 2, ch. 17).
Giant squid seize the Nautilus. A crewman is lost in the fight (Part 2, ch. 18).
In the Gulf Stream (Part 2, ch. 19).
The Nautilus skirts the southern edge of the Newfoundland fishing banks, then turns east over the Atlantic plateau (Part 2, ch. 20).
Heading east along the telegraph plateau, Aronnax sights the submarine cable about 500 miles from its Newfoundland landing at Heart’s Content (Part 2, ch. 20).
Nemo stops over the French ship sunk in 1794, 'seventy-four years ago, day for day'. The next day a warship hunts the Nautilus, and he sinks it (Part 2, ch. 20–21).
After some weeks adrift in the north, the three escape in the dinghy as the Nautilus is drawn into the whirlpool. They wake in a fisherman's hut in the Lofoten Islands (Part 2, ch. 22–23).
